gameOver.message: Player DSV3 Stoic is the winner

annotations.description: Playing Command Tower on turn 1 when there are no 1-mana plays available wastes the untapped advantage. The player has two taplands (Woodland Stream, Memorial to Genius) that could be played on turn 1 at no tempo cost, saving Command Tower for a later turn where entering untapped matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Command Tower on turn 1 with no plays available.
annotations.betterLine: Play Woodland Stream (or Memorial to Genius) tapped on turn 1, then play Command Tower untapped on turn 2 alongside Khalni Heart Expedition or save it for a turn where the untapped entry matters.

annotations.description: Playing Mystic Monastery (enters tapped) instead of Plains (enters untapped) on turn 1 means DSV3 Stoic cannot cast Faithless Looting on turn 2 if they draw a non-tapped land, since Mystic Monastery won't produce red until next turn anyway. However, more importantly, Plains entering untapped would leave mana available, and on turn 2, playing Mystic Monastery tapped while having Plains untapped would allow casting Faithless Looting turn 2. With Mystic Monastery first, turn 2 they play Plains untapped and can still cast Faithless Looting - so the sequencing is actually similar. The real issue is that Plains doesn't produce red for Faithless Looting. Mystic Monastery produces U/R/W, so playing it turn 1 (tapped) means it's ready turn 2 for Faithless Looting if they play any other land. Playing Plains first means they'd need another red source for Faithless Looting. Actually, Mystic Monastery is likely the correct play here since it enables Faithless Looting on turn 2 with any untapped land. However, Prairie Stream checks for two basic lands - playing Plains first would help toward that. With only one basic (Plains) in hand, Prairie Stream will enter tapped regardless. So Mystic Monastery turn 1 is reasonable for enabling turn 2 Faithless Looting.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mystic Monastery (enters tapped, produces U/R/W)
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable - Mystic Monastery enables Faithless Looting on turn 2. No clear better line.

annotations.description: With Growth Spiral in hand (an instant that draws a card and puts a land into play), the optimal turn 2 play is to play Island untapped, then cast Growth Spiral using Command Tower + Island, draw a card, and potentially put Woodland Stream or Memorial to Genius onto the battlefield as the extra land drop. This would net an extra card and an extra land compared to just playing Woodland Stream tapped. By playing Woodland Stream (which enters tapped), the player has no untapped mana to cast Growth Spiral this turn, wasting a full turn of development.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Woodland Stream (enters tapped), leaving no untapped lands to cast Growth Spiral.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island untapped, then cast Growth Spiral using Command Tower + Island to draw a card and potentially put an additional land (like Woodland Stream or Memorial to Genius) onto the battlefield.

annotations.description: Devil's Play has flashback ({X}{R}{R}{R}), making it the ideal card to discard to Faithless Looting since it retains full value from the graveyard. This is a core synergy of Faithless Looting - discarding cards with flashback or graveyard value. Boros Guildgate, while a tapped land, is permanently lost when discarded.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Boros Guildgate as first discard to Faithless Looting
annotations.betterLine: Discard Devil's Play as one of the two cards, since it has flashback and can be cast from the graveyard later, preserving its full value while getting maximum benefit from Faithless Looting's draw-discard effect.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic is discarding Azorius Chancery to Faithless Looting. While Azorius Chancery enters tapped and bounces a land, it's a dual-mana producing land that would be very valuable in a deck that needs W, U, and R mana. Looking at their hand after the first discard (which we don't see but this is the second pick), they still have Boros Guildgate, Prairie Stream, and Island as land options. However, Azorius Chancery produces both W and U mana every turn - it's effectively a ramp card. Meanwhile, cards like Magmaquake and Devil's Play are X-spells that are very expensive and less useful in the early game. Discarding Magmaquake (which requires a lot of mana to be effective and is situational) or Devil's Play (which has flashback so it can be cast from the graveyard anyway) would be significantly better choices. Devil's Play specifically has flashback {X}{R}{R}{R}, meaning discarding it actually enables casting it later from the graveyard - it's practically designed to be discarded.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Azorius Chancery, a dual-mana-producing land, to Faithless Looting.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Devil's Play, which has flashback and can be cast from the graveyard, making it an ideal discard target for Faithless Looting. This preserves the valuable mana-fixing bounce land.

annotations.description: Player incorrectly believed Prairie Stream would enter untapped (stating they have 2 basics), but they only control 1 basic land (Plains). Mystic Monastery is not basic. Prairie Stream enters tapped, meaning they waste their turn 3 with no play, whereas Island would enter untapped allowing them to cast Armillary Sphere this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Prairie Stream (which enters tapped due to only 1 basic land), leaving them unable to cast anything on turn 3.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (enters untapped), then cast Armillary Sphere for 2 mana, getting the artifact online a full turn earlier for mana fixing and development.

annotations.description: Passed the turn without playing a land despite having Island and Lonely Sandbar in hand. On turn 3 with a hand full of expensive cards (Terastodon at 8 mana, Hydra Broodmaster at 6, Deekah at 5, Nissa's Expedition at 5), missing a land drop significantly delays the game plan. Additionally, could have deployed Sequence Engine this turn for 3 mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any card or land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island as land for turn, then cast Sequence Engine (2G) using Forest, Forest, Island. This puts 4 lands on board and deploys a useful artifact. Alternatively, play Lonely Sandbar (enters tapped) and still cast Sequence Engine with the 3 untapped lands.

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge has 3 lands in play and a hand full of expensive cards (Terastodon at 8, Hydra Broodmaster at 6, Deekah at 5, Nissa's Expedition at 5). Sequence Engine costs 3 mana and could be played this turn, providing a mana sink and utility for later turns. Instead, the player passed without playing anything, wasting 3 available mana. Lonely Sandbar could also be cycled if they don't want to play it as a tapped land, but playing Sequence Engine is the clear best use of mana here since it costs exactly 3 and provides future value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing anything, leaving 3 mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sequence Engine for {2}{G} using all three available lands. This develops the board and provides a useful mana sink for future turns while working toward the game plan of creating Fractal tokens.

annotations.description: GLM47 ESPN played Forest as their land drop instead of Mountain, then will presumably want to cast Animar (GUR) this turn. With Mountain + Island + Gruul Signet already on board, playing Forest gives access to G (Forest), R (Mountain), U (Island), and RG (Gruul Signet via 1+tap). To cast Animar (GUR), they need G, U, and R. They can do this either way: with Forest they tap Forest(G), Island(U), Mountain(R). With Mountain they'd tap Mountain(R), Island(U), and use Gruul Signet (1+tap for G). Both work for casting Animar. However, the real issue is sequencing: they should cast Animar BEFORE playing the land, or at minimum consider playing Mountain instead of Forest since they already have green access through Gruul Signet, and having two Mountains provides better red mana redundancy for future plays like Colossal Might or Devil's Play. The choice of Forest over Mountain is slightly suboptimal given existing mana base.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Playing Mountain would have been slightly better since Gruul Signet already provides green mana, and having additional red sources supports future plays like Colossal Might. Either way, Animar can still be cast this turn.

annotations.description: Casting Animar before Lightning Greaves means Animar is vulnerable to removal for a full turn cycle around the table (3 opponents). Lightning Greaves costs 2 mana to cast and 0 to equip. The correct sequence is to cast Lightning Greaves first (2 mana from Gruul Signet + 1 land), then cast Animar with remaining mana (GUR from the three lands), and immediately equip Greaves for free, giving Animar shroud and haste. With the current play, Animar sits exposed. Animar does have protection from white and black, but is still vulnerable to red, green, and blue removal, as well as colorless effects.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Animar, Soul of Elements without first deploying Lightning Greaves for protection.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana via Gruul Signet), then cast Animar (G from Forest, U from Island, R from Mountain), then equip Lightning Greaves for free to give Animar shroud and haste immediately.

annotations.description: The player's reasoning mentions wanting to activate Khalni Heart Expedition, but Khalni Heart Expedition is in their hand, not on the battlefield - it hasn't been cast yet. They chose to cast Sol Ring instead of playing Forest first. Playing Forest first would be better sequencing: it uses the free land drop, then they could cast Sol Ring with the Command Tower (untapped), and still have mana available. More importantly, they should play the Forest first to have 6 lands, then cast Khalni Heart Expedition (which costs 1G) with remaining mana, so it can start accumulating quest counters. By casting Sol Ring first, they use Command Tower's mana on Sol Ring, but they could have played the land first and still cast Sol Ring with Sol Ring's own mana not being available yet. Actually, looking more carefully: Command Tower is untapped, and they have Forest in hand. The correct sequence is: Play Forest from hand (free land drop), then cast Sol Ring using Command Tower. This gives the same result. But actually both sequences work - play Forest, tap Command Tower for Sol Ring; or cast Sol Ring tapping Command Tower, then play Forest. The end state is the same. However, the reasoning is confused about Khalni Heart Expedition being on the battlefield when it's actually in hand, though this doesn't affect the actual play made. The real question is whether Sol Ring is the right play here versus casting Khalni Heart Expedition. With Sol Ring + Forest played, they'll have access to 7 mana next turn (5 lands + Sol Ring). With Khalni Heart Expedition instead, they'd build toward future ramp. Sol Ring is generally the stronger play for immediate mana acceleration toward Avenger of Zendikar. The play itself (Sol Ring) is reasonable, but playing the Forest first before casting Sol Ring is slightly better sequencing in general (land before spells), though in this specific case the end result is identical.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sol Ring before playing Forest from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first (free land drop), then cast Sol Ring with Command Tower. The end board state is the same, but proper sequencing dictates playing lands before casting spells to preserve information and options.

annotations.description: The player passed without playing Lonely Sandbar as their land drop or casting Sequence Engine with 4 available mana. With expensive cards like Terastodon (8), Ezuri's Predation (8), and Nissa's Expedition (5) in hand, missing a land drop delays their game plan significantly. Sequence Engine could also be deployed for future value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any cards or making a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Lonely Sandbar as the land for turn (enters tapped, so sets up 5 lands next turn), and cast Sequence Engine with the remaining 4 untapped mana (costs {2}{G}).

annotations.description: Passed the turn with 4 untapped lands and castable Sequence Engine (2G) in hand, wasting an entire turn of mana and board development. Could have also cycled Lonely Sandbar with remaining mana to dig for better cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, leaving all 4 lands untapped.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sequence Engine for {2}{G} (using 2 Islands + 1 Forest), then cycle Lonely Sandbar with the remaining Island to draw a card. This develops the board and replaces a card.

annotations.betterLine: Search for Baloth Woodcrasher, which is castable much sooner, and has incredible synergy with Explosive Vegetation in hand plus Lightning Greaves for a potential hasty 12/12 trampler

annotations.description: With only 7 mana available (5 lands + Sol Ring producing 7 mana total), the player cast Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait (6 mana) from the command zone, leaving only 1 mana open. However, the reasoning text says they planned to play a land and Khalni Heart Expedition, but they actually cast their 6-mana commander instead. More importantly, casting Aesi before playing a land for the turn means they miss the landfall trigger from their land drop this turn. They should have played their land first (getting a free card draw from Aesi's landfall), but they can't because Aesi isn't on the battlefield yet when they'd want to play the land. The bigger issue is sequencing: they had Harmonize (4 mana, draw 3), Simic Signet (2 mana for ramp), Khalni Heart Expedition (2 mana for future ramp), and Seer's Sundial (4 mana) as alternatives. Playing Simic Signet + Khalni Heart Expedition (4 mana total) or Harmonize would have been better tempo plays, setting up to cast Aesi next turn with more mana and getting the landfall trigger. Casting Aesi into a board where GLM47 ESPN has an active Animar and creatures (suggesting removal or pressure coming) with no protection and leaving only 1 mana open (can't even use Simic Charm to protect it) is risky.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait from command zone for 6 mana, leaving 1 mana open with no way to protect it.
annotations.betterLine: Play Simic Signet (2 mana) + Khalni Heart Expedition (2 mana) or Seer's Sundial (4 mana), then cast Aesi next turn with more mana available and protection from Simic Charm. Alternatively, cast Harmonize to draw 3 cards and find more resources before committing the commander.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Izzet Locket for 3 mana to accelerate toward Pristine Angel and power up future X spells (Magmaquake/Devil's Play), then play a land from hand

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge has 4 lands and no mana rocks, with Sol Ring in hand. Sol Ring costs only 1 mana and provides 2 colorless mana, which would massively accelerate their ability to cast expensive spells like Terastodon (8 mana), Hydra Broodmaster (6 mana), Ezuri's Predation (8 mana), and Deekah (5 mana). Discarding Lonely Sandbar instead of playing it or keeping it means they're at a hand size issue (9 cards, need to discard to 7), but the real blunder is that Sol Ring should have been cast during their main phase for 1 mana, not discarded or kept in hand requiring a discard of something else. Looking at the board state, all 4 lands are tapped, suggesting they already spent their mana this turn. But Sol Ring costs only {1} - they should have cast it. The fact that Sol Ring is still in hand at end of turn with lands that were available suggests they failed to cast Sol Ring during their turn, which is a significant missed opportunity for ramp. Additionally, Lonely Sandbar could have been cycled for {U} to draw a card instead of being discarded, though all Islands appear tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Lonely Sandbar to hand size, while Sol Ring remained uncast in hand
annotations.betterLine: Should have cast Sol Ring during the main phase for {1} (it's one of the best mana rocks in the game). This would have also reduced hand size by one, potentially avoiding the need to discard at all or allowing them to keep Lonely Sandbar. With Sol Ring on board, they could cast Deekah or Nissa's Expedition much sooner.

annotations.description: Casting Explosive Vegetation instead of leveraging Animar's cost reduction to deploy multiple cheap creatures. Both could be cast this turn for 4 mana total, giving Animar 2 counters (reducing future creature costs by 2), protecting Animar with shroud/haste, and enabling card draw from combat damage via Edric.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Explosive Vegetation for 4 mana to ramp by 2 lands.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Edric, Spymaster of Trest for GU (discounted by Animar's counter), putting a second counter on Animar. Then cast Lightning Greaves for 2, equip to Animar for free. Attack with Animar and Fierce Empath to draw cards via Edric. This builds Animar's counters faster toward casting Artisan of Kozilek while generating card advantage.

annotations.actionTaken: Selected Forest (with stated intent to select two Forests total)

annotations.betterLine: Cast Khalni Heart Expedition (1G) first using available mana, then play Vivid Grove to trigger both Aesi's draw AND a quest counter on Khalni Heart Expedition, then play a second land if available for another counter.

Playing Seer's Sundial (4 mana) now would set up additional card draw from future landfall triggers alongside Aesi, compounding value. Holding up Simic Charm with no colored mana available is pointless - they should have cast Seer's Sundial using Sol Ring + 2 other mana after untapping, maximizing future landfall value.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast anything, planning to hold up Simic Charm for interaction, but all colored mana sources are tapped.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Seer's Sundial for 4 mana (Sol Ring + 2 lands), then play lands on subsequent turns to trigger both Aesi and Sundial for massive card advantage. The Simic Charm can be held up on future turns when mana is actually available.

Sol Ring costs only 1 mana and would immediately accelerate mana production by 2 colorless, enabling much faster deployment of the expensive cards in hand (Terastodon at 8, Hydra Broodmaster at 6, Ezuri's Predation at 8, Deekah at 5, Nissa's Expedition at 5). annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any abilities or casting spells, allowing Aesi to continue generating card advantage.

Lightning Greaves (2 mana) would protect Animar and give it haste (already has it but shroud is valuable protection). Prophetic Prism (2 mana) draws a card and fixes mana. Edric, Spymaster of Trest (3 mana) would let them draw cards when their creatures deal combat damage. annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana) to give Animar shroud protection, cast Prophetic Prism (2 mana) to draw a card and fix mana, cast Edric, Spymaster of Trest (3 mana) to reward combat damage with card draw, equip Greaves to Animar (free), then attack with Fierce Empath into an opponent to potentially draw a card off Edric.

With Aesi allowing extra land drops and 3 lands in hand, casting Seer's Sundial first (4 mana from 8 available) would let them get Sundial triggers on each subsequent land drop. Playing Island first wastes at least one Sundial trigger (pay 2 to draw a card).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island as the first action of the turn, before casting Seer's Sundial.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Seer's Sundial first (4 mana), then play the three lands (Island, Island, Vivid Creek) to maximize landfall triggers from both Aesi and Seer's Sundial, potentially drawing 2+ extra cards.

annotations.actionTaken: Played Vivid Creek (enters tapped) as the first land drop of the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first (untapped, providing immediate mana), then play Vivid Creek as the second land drop via Aesi. This maximizes available mana for casting spells this turn.

annotations.description: With Aesi on the battlefield (play an additional land + landfall draw), casting Cultivate before Avenger of Zendikar would have been superior. Cultivate puts a land onto the battlefield tapped (triggering Aesi's landfall to draw a card) and puts another land into hand. Then playing the Island from hand triggers another Aesi landfall draw. After that, casting Avenger would create tokens equal to the higher land count (8+1+1=10 lands instead of 8), and the player would have drawn 2 extra cards and have more land drops available to pump the plants. By casting Avenger first with only 8 lands, they get 8 plant tokens instead of potentially 10, and miss the opportunity to sequence land ramp before the token-creating spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Avenger of Zendikar immediately, creating 8 plant tokens (for 8 lands in play).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cultivate first (searching for two basics, putting one onto battlefield tapped triggering Aesi draw, one to hand), then play the Island from hand (triggering another Aesi draw), then cast Avenger of Zendikar to create 10 plant tokens with more cards in hand for future turns.

Playing the land first ensures no missed land drop and leaves more mana open after casting the Angel. Additionally, with Aesi on the board for Gem25P Coach generating card advantage, and Animar growing for GLM47 ESPN, holding up Magmaquake or Mass Diminish as answers might be more impactful. However, Pristine Angel is a strong defensive creature that's hard to remove while untapped, so this isn't clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pristine Angel for 4WW using available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first (ensuring the land drop), then evaluate whether casting Pristine Angel or holding up mana for Mass Diminish/Magmaquake is better positioned. Pristine Angel is reasonable but playing the land first is strictly better sequencing.

annotations.description: Golden Ratio draws cards based on different powers among creatures you control. Qwen3 Sarge controls only Adrix and Nev (2/2), so Golden Ratio draws only 1 card for 3 mana (1GU). Meanwhile, Sol Ring costs 1 mana and would immediately accelerate future turns, and could have been cast first before Golden Ratio to use remaining mana more efficiently. More importantly, casting Sol Ring (1 mana) first leaves 4 mana open, which could cast Sequence Engine (2G) and still have mana left, or cast Nissa's Expedition with convoke. The sequencing of Sol Ring before other spells is almost always correct when you have it available, as it provides mana acceleration for the same turn and future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Golden Ratio for 3 mana (1GU), drawing only 1 card since only one distinct power (2) exists among controlled creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sol Ring first (1 mana), then use the additional mana to cast Sequence Engine (2G) or Nissa's Expedition (with convoke from Adrix and Nev to reduce cost). Golden Ratio with only 1 distinct power is very inefficient at 3 mana for 1 card draw.

annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Fierce Empath (1/1) with Plant Token (0/1), letting Animar (2/2) through for 2 damage
annotations.betterLine: Block Animar, Soul of Elements (2/2) with the Plant Token to prevent 2 damage instead of 1, letting the 1/1 Fierce Empath through instead

annotations.description: During the combat phase (after attacks), Gem25P Coach had the option to activate Memorial to Genius (sacrifice to draw 2 cards) or cast Simic Charm as an instant. With 8 cards in hand and needing to discard down to 7 at end of turn, activating Memorial to Genius would have been wasteful at this exact moment since they'd just discard more cards. However, Simic Charm could have been cast for value (e.g., +3/+3 on Aesi for extra combat damage, or hexproof to protect permanents). The player passed without using either option, and then had to discard down to 7 cards anyway. While Memorial activation would have been bad timing (already over hand size), casting Simic Charm for +3/+3 on Aesi during combat could have dealt extra damage. The reasoning given ('stuck in a time loop') suggests confusion about the game state rather than strategic decision-making.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any instants or activating abilities during combat, then discarded to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Could have cast Simic Charm for +3/+3 on Aesi to deal extra combat damage, since a card would need to be discarded anyway at end of turn.

annotations.description: Slinn Voda is an 8/8 that bounces all non-sea-creature permanents when kicked, which is a powerful finisher. With Aesi on board generating extra land drops and card draw, reaching 10 mana for a kicked Slinn Voda is very achievable. Discarding it removes a key win condition from hand. Meanwhile, Eternal Witness in hand can recur cards from the graveyard, but the most impactful card to recur would be Slinn Voda itself if discarded - which is circular and wasteful. A basic Forest or Island is the obvious discard since the player already has 7 lands on board and Cultivate to find more.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Slinn Voda, the Rising Deep - a powerful 8/8 finisher with a game-changing kicked ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard a basic Forest or Island instead, as the player already has 7 lands in play plus Cultivate and Sol Ring for ramp. Keeping Slinn Voda as a late-game finisher that bounces opponents' boards (especially threatening against Qwen3's Adrix and Nev and GLM47's Animar) would be far more impactful than an extra basic land.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic passed their precombat main phase without playing a land, despite having both Island and Mountain in hand. They have 6 untapped lands + Izzet Locket and need to build toward casting Pristine Skywise (4WU) and maximizing X spells like Magmaquake and Devil's Play. Missing a land drop when holding lands is always wasteful.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed precombat main phase without playing a land or any spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (to support Pristine Skywise's UW cost and future Mass Diminish flashback) to reach 9 mana sources, then pass or consider casting Pristine Skywise if the mana works out with Izzet Locket providing the needed colors.

annotations.description: Attacking with Adrix and Nev, Twincasters (2/2) is risky and provides minimal value. Adrix and Nev is a key engine piece that doubles token creation, which synergizes with multiple cards in hand (Hydra Broodmaster, Ezuri's Predation, Spawning Kraken, Deekah). Risking it in combat for 2 damage is poor value. While no obvious blockers are untapped right now, the 2 damage is negligible in a 4-player game where opponents are at 30-40 life, and losing this creature to a combat trick or removal would be devastating to the game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Adrix and Nev, Twincasters.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Adrix and Nev back to protect this critical engine piece. The 2 damage is insignificant compared to the risk of losing the token-doubling effect needed for Hydra Broodmaster, Ezuri's Predation, and other token generators in hand.

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge has 5 lands and Adrix and Nev on the battlefield, with Sol Ring in hand. Sol Ring costs only 1 mana and provides 2 colorless mana, which is one of the best mana accelerants in the game. They also have Sequence Engine (costs 2) and Plaxcaster Frogling (costs 3, enters with +1/+1 counters and provides protection). Playing Sol Ring now would cost just 1 mana and leave 4 mana open for Plaxcaster Frogling (3 mana) or Sequence Engine (2 mana), or both if Sol Ring is played first (1 mana for Sol Ring, then 4 lands + Sol Ring = 6 mana remaining, enough for both Sequence Engine at 2 and Plaxcaster Frogling at 3 = 5 total). By passing without playing anything, they waste mana and will have to discard down to 7, losing cards unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any spells, resulting in having to discard cards from a full hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Sol Ring (1 mana), then play Sequence Engine (2 mana) and Plaxcaster Frogling (3 mana from remaining lands + Sol Ring). This deploys three permanents, uses all available mana, and avoids discarding valuable cards like Hydra Broodmaster or Spawning Kraken.

annotations.description: Spitting Image has Retrace, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard by discarding a land card. Discarding it to hand size isn't terrible since it can still be used from the graveyard, but the player has Aesi (which draws extra cards and enables extra land drops) making lands very valuable. However, Spitting Image with Retrace actually works FROM the graveyard, so discarding it preserves its utility. The real question is whether another card like Seer's Sundial (4 mana artifact that costs 2 more each trigger) might have been a better discard given the player already has Aesi for card draw. With Aesi already providing landfall card draw, Seer's Sundial is somewhat redundant and expensive to use.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spitting Image to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discarding Seer's Sundial would have been better since Aesi already provides landfall-based card draw, making the Sundial redundant. Spitting Image in hand is more flexible than in the graveyard (doesn't require discarding a land to cast), though Retrace does preserve some utility.

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge has Sol Ring in hand and 4 lands + Adrix and Nev on board. Sol Ring costs 1 mana and adds 2 colorless, which would enable casting both Plaxcaster Frogling (1GU) and potentially another spell this turn or next turn. By casting Plaxcaster Frogling first without playing Sol Ring, they miss the opportunity to have Sol Ring's mana available for this turn's remaining plays or to deploy more efficiently. Sol Ring should almost always be cast as early as possible since it's pure mana acceleration. With Sol Ring down first, they'd have 6 mana available (4 lands + Sol Ring) which could cast Plaxcaster Frogling and still have mana open, or even cast Deekah (4U) instead. At minimum, Sol Ring should be cast before Plaxcaster Frogling to maximize mana available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Plaxcaster Frogling (spending 3 of 4 available mana) without first casting Sol Ring
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sol Ring first (1 mana), then cast Plaxcaster Frogling (3 mana from remaining 3 lands + Sol Ring), leaving Sol Ring on board for future turns with extra mana still available this turn

annotations.description: GLM47 ESPN passed their precombat main phase with multiple productive plays available: Simic Growth Chamber as a land drop, Lightning Greaves (2 mana) to protect Animar, and Edric (reduced cost with Animar counters) for card advantage. Missing the land drop alone is a significant tempo loss, and failing to deploy Lightning Greaves to protect the key Animar is a meaningful strategic error.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any spells or lands in precombat main.
annotations.betterLine: Play Simic Growth Chamber (bouncing a basic), cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana) to protect Animar with shroud, then potentially cast Edric before or after combat to start drawing cards off combat damage.

annotations.description: Activating Khalni Heart Expedition while Avenger of Zendikar is still on the stack means the two lands enter before Avenger resolves. This gives 2 extra Plant tokens from Avenger's ETB, but misses putting +1/+1 counters on ALL Plants from Avenger's landfall trigger (which would fire twice for the two lands). With ~8 lands already in play creating ~8 Plants, getting +1/+1 counters on all of them twice is likely more valuable than 2 additional 0/1 tokens. They still had 3 lands in hand plus Aesi's extra land drop to trigger landfall after Avenger resolved.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Khalni Heart Expedition before Avenger of Zendikar resolved, putting two lands into play before Plant tokens were created.
annotations.betterLine: Let Avenger of Zendikar resolve first to create Plant tokens, then activate Khalni Heart Expedition to put two lands into play, triggering Avenger's landfall to put +1/+1 counters on each Plant twice, plus Aesi's landfall for 2 card draws.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic cast Sol Ring before playing a land. They have Boros Garrison, Island, and Mountain in hand. Playing Boros Garrison first (which enters tapped and bounces a land) would be optimal since it doesn't cost mana and should be done before spending mana on spells. More importantly, casting Sol Ring before playing a land is a sequencing error - they should play their land drop first to maximize information and mana availability. With 8 lands already on board and Sol Ring costing only 1 mana, the order matters less than usual, but it's still slightly suboptimal sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sol Ring before making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Boros Garrison first (bouncing a tapped Plains), then cast Sol Ring with the remaining untapped mana, giving access to more mana this turn for follow-up plays like Pristine Skywise

annotations.description: GLM47 ESPN attacked Gem25P Coach who has an untapped Aesi (5/5) that can block and kill either attacker, while Qwen3 Sarge has no untapped blockers (both Adrix and Nev and Plaxcaster Frogling are tapped), guaranteeing all damage connects.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem25P Coach, risking creatures being blocked and killed by the 5/5 Aesi
annotations.betterLine: Attack Qwen3 Sarge who has no untapped blockers, guaranteeing all combat damage connects safely

annotations.description: Gem25P Coach had multiple 1/2 Plant tokens (from Avenger of Zendikar landfall triggers giving +1/+1 counters, though the board shows them as Plant Tokens) and Aesi (5/5) available to block. Animar, Soul of Elements is a key threat that grows with each creature cast - letting it through unblocked means it deals 2 damage AND survives to continue accumulating counters. Meanwhile, a Plant token was used to block the much less threatening Fierce Empath (1/1). The correct play was to block Animar with a Plant token (or even Aesi) to kill it, since Animar is far more dangerous long-term. Letting Animar survive and deal damage while blocking the insignificant Fierce Empath is a clear misprioritization of threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Fierce Empath with a Plant Token but left Animar, Soul of Elements unblocked, taking 2 damage and letting Animar survive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Animar, Soul of Elements with a Plant Token (and optionally also block Fierce Empath with another Plant Token). Killing Animar is far more important than blocking a 1/1 Fierce Empath, as Animar snowballs with +1/+1 counters from every creature cast.

annotations.description: With Aesi in play, each land drop generates an extra card draw, making lands more valuable than usual. Sporemound is arguably the weakest card in hand - a 5-mana 3/3 that makes 1/1 tokens is lower impact than the extra Aesi trigger from a Forest. The player also has Cultivate to find basics, which somewhat mitigates losing the Forest, but keeping maximum land density with Aesi is generally preferred.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Forest
annotations.betterLine: Discard Sporemound, as it's the lowest-impact card in hand. With Aesi in play, the extra Forest provides a guaranteed card draw trigger, which is worth more than Sporemound's modest board presence.

annotations.description: Playing Boros Garrison enters tapped and bounces a land, costing significant tempo when GLM47 ESPN is at 6 life and DSV3 Stoic has Devil's Play in hand. An untapped basic land would have provided more mana this turn for potential plays like Pristine Skywise or burning out the low-life opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Boros Garrison, which enters tapped and bounces a land back to hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (or Mountain/Plains) untapped to maximize available mana this turn, enabling casting Pristine Skywise or using Devil's Play to pressure GLM47 ESPN at 6 life.

annotations.description: Bounced Prairie Stream (a dual land providing W/U) instead of a basic Plains when Boros Garrison already covers the white mana. Prairie Stream enters untapped with their basics, but a basic Plains is more redundant given Boros Garrison's {R}{W} production. They have Pristine Skywise and Mass Diminish in hand needing blue mana, making the U/W dual more valuable on board than an extra Plains.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Prairie Stream to hand with Boros Garrison's ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Bounce a basic Plains instead, since Boros Garrison already provides white mana and keeping Prairie Stream on board preserves blue mana access for Pristine Skywise and Mass Diminish

annotations.description: GLM47 ESPN is at 6 life with no flying blockers. DSV3 Stoic has Pristine Angel (4/4 flying) and Devil's Play in hand. Attacking ESPN for 4 (to 2 life) then casting Devil's Play for X=2 (using Mountain + Sol Ring for {2}{R}) would eliminate a player this turn. Instead, they attacked Gem25P Coach at 24 life, dealing only chip damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem25P Coach (24 life) with Pristine Angel for 4 damage
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 ESPN (6 life) with Pristine Angel for 4, then cast Devil's Play X=2 post-combat to eliminate ESPN entirely, removing a player from the game

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge passed the turn with 8 mana available (3 Islands, 2 Forests, Sol Ring) and multiple castable spells in hand, deploying nothing. Spawning Kraken (6 mana), Deekah (5 mana), Replication Technique (5 mana), and Nissa's Expedition (5 mana with convoke potential) were all castable. With GLM47 ESPN at 1 life and needing board presence, wasting an entire turn's worth of mana is a significant tempo loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting any spells despite having 8 available mana and multiple castable options.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Spawning Kraken (6 mana) to establish a major threat, or Deekah, Fractal Theorist (5 mana) to start generating token value from future spells, or Nissa's Expedition to ramp toward Ezuri's Predation.

annotations.description: Gem25P Coach is sending Avenger of Zendikar (5/5) at GLM47 ESPN who is at 1 life, when a single Plant token could deal lethal. This wastes the Avenger's 5 power that could have been directed at Qwen3 Sarge (40 life) or DSV3 Stoic (40 life). Since Qwen3 Sarge's creatures are tapped, sending Aesi + Avenger at Sarge would deal 10 unblocked damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Avenger of Zendikar to attack GLM47 ESPN (1 life), overkilling by 4+ damage
annotations.betterLine: Send a single Plant token at GLM47 ESPN for lethal, and direct Avenger of Zendikar and Aesi at Qwen3 Sarge (or DSV3 Stoic) to apply meaningful pressure to the remaining opponents

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic casts Storm Herd for 10 mana (8WW) to create 40 1/1 Pegasus tokens with flying while at 40 life. However, Qwen3 Sarge has Adrix and Nev, Twincasters on the board which could double token creation if they copy Storm Herd somehow, and more importantly, the opponent Qwen3 Sarge still has resources. The main concern is that DSV3 Stoic should consider whether to play a land first (they have Island, Mountain, Plains, Prairie Stream in hand) before casting Storm Herd. With 8 lands on board, they need all 8 to cast Storm Herd (8WW requires exactly Sol Ring + Izzet Locket + lands). Looking at the mana: Sol Ring (2 colorless), Izzet Locket (1 U or R), Mystic Monastery (U/R/W), Plains (W), Mountain (R), Plains (W), Island (U), Pristine Angel is a creature not a land. That's 7 lands + Sol Ring + Izzet Locket = 9 mana sources producing at most 10 mana. They need 8WW - they can get WW from two Plains, and the rest from other sources. This works. But they didn't play a land first. Playing a land before casting Storm Herd costs nothing and would give them more mana available for future turns. This is a minor sequencing error - they should play a land (like Prairie Stream or Island) before casting Storm Herd.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Storm Herd without first playing a land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (e.g., Prairie Stream or Island) first, then cast Storm Herd. The land drop is free and would provide additional mana on future turns.

annotations.description: Plant tokens cannot block Pristine Angel because it has flying and plants lack flying/reach. The player attempted an illegal block instead of using Simic Charm to bounce the attacking Pristine Angel, which would have saved 4 damage at 18 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to block flying Pristine Angel with a ground-only Plant token, which is an illegal block
annotations.betterLine: Cast Simic Charm choosing the bounce mode to return Pristine Angel to DSV3 Stoic's hand, preventing 4 damage and temporarily removing the threat

annotations.description: With 8 mana available (4 forests, 3 islands, Sol Ring), Qwen3 Sarge chose Hydra Broodmaster (4GG = 6 mana) over potentially more impactful plays. Nissa's Expedition with convoke could ramp significantly by tapping Adrix and Nev and Plaxcaster Frogling to help cast it, fetching 2 lands and setting up for Ezuri's Predation next turn. Replication Technique (4U = 5 mana) copying Adrix and Nev (doubling token production even further) or Plaxcaster Frogling could also be strong. However, Hydra Broodmaster is a 7/7 that threatens a massive token army later with its monstrosity ability, especially with Adrix and Nev doubling the tokens. The main concern is that casting Hydra Broodmaster leaves only 2 mana open and doesn't immediately impact the board, while Replication Technique on Adrix and Nev would set up exponential token doubling. With only two opponents remaining (GLM47 ESPN is at -9hp, eliminated), and Gem25P Coach at 14hp with Aesi on board, the Hydra Broodmaster's monstrosity activation won't come online for a while. Replication Technique copying Adrix and Nev would quadruple future tokens and could be game-winning with Ezuri's Predation.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hydra Broodmaster (6 mana), leaving 2 mana unused with no immediate board impact beyond a vanilla 7/7.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Replication Technique (5 mana) targeting Adrix and Nev, Twincasters to create a copy (quadrupling future token creation), then use remaining 3 mana for other plays. This sets up a devastating Ezuri's Predation on a future turn with quadrupled tokens.

annotations.description: Declined to graft a +1/+1 counter onto Hydra Broodmaster. This is a missed opportunity because having a +1/+1 counter on Hydra Broodmaster enables Plaxcaster Frogling's activated ability to grant it shroud, protecting a key threat that can generate massive tokens via Monstrosity. The +1/+1 stat boost is marginal, but the shroud protection is meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined the Graft trigger, leaving Hydra Broodmaster without a +1/+1 counter.
annotations.betterLine: Accept the Graft trigger to place a +1/+1 counter on Hydra Broodmaster, enabling Plaxcaster Frogling to grant it shroud protection for {2}.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic has Pristine Angel (4/4 flying) on board and Pristine Skywise (6/4 flying) in hand. Gem25P Coach is at exactly 10 life with no flying blockers (Aesi is a 5/5 ground creature). Casting Pristine Skywise and attacking with both flyers would deal exactly 10 damage for lethal. DSV3 Stoic has the mana: Plains+Plains+Island+Mystic Monastery+Sol Ring+Izzet Locket covers the 4WU cost. Instead, they passed without doing anything in precombat main.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the precombat main phase without casting any spells or playing a land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain, cast Pristine Skywise (4WU) using available mana, then go to combat and attack Gem25P Coach with both Pristine Angel (4/4) and Pristine Skywise (6/4) for exactly 10 flying damage = lethal.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic passed the turn without playing a land (has Mountain and Plains in hand) and without casting Pristine Skywise (6/4 flyer for 4WU, which is castable with available mana). In a 1v1 against a 40-life opponent, deploying a 6/4 flying threat and making a land drop are both important to establish a clock.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing any spells or lands in postcombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain (or Plains) as a land drop, then cast Pristine Skywise (4WU) using available mana to establish a flying threat alongside Pristine Angel.

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic cast Pristine Skywise before playing a land from hand. They have Mountain and Plains in hand and appear to have not yet made their land drop this turn. Playing a land first is free and would give them an additional mana source, which could matter for future plays or if they draw into something useful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pristine Skywise without first playing a land from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (or Mountain) first, then cast Pristine Skywise with the additional mana available

annotations.description: DSV3 Stoic cast Ghostly Prison before playing a land. They had Mountain and Plains in hand and hadn't used their land drop yet. Playing a land first (likely Mountain for future Devil's Play/Increasing Vengeance flexibility) before casting spells is standard correct sequencing, as it maximizes available mana and preserves options.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ghostly Prison without first making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain (or Plains) first, then cast Ghostly Prison

annotations.description: If Hydra Broodmaster is on the battlefield (implied by being in the choices), declining to activate its Monstrosity ability with Adrix and Nev (token doubler) on the field is a missed opportunity to build a massive board. With available mana, they could create multiple large Hydra tokens doubled by Adrix and Nev, putting enormous pressure on DSV3 Stoic who only has Pristine Angel as a threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Activate Hydra Broodmaster's Monstrosity ability for X=2 or X=3 (depending on available mana), creating doubled tokens via Adrix and Nev to overwhelm the opponent

annotations.description: Qwen3 Sarge skipped attacking the sole remaining opponent (DSV3 Stoic at 28 life) when DSV3 Stoic was completely tapped out. Pristine Angel can only block one attacker, meaning at least two creatures would deal unblocked damage. With Hydra Broodmaster (7/7), Adrix and Nev (2/2), and Plaxcaster Frogling, attacking would push through significant damage (likely 9+ points) with no risk since Stoic has no mana available for tricks.
annotations.actionTaken: Skipped the attack phase entirely, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures. Pristine Angel (protection from colors while untapped) can block one colored creature without taking damage, but the remaining attackers get through for significant damage. Even in the worst case, this is free damage against a tapped-out opponent in a 1v1 situation.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Hydra Broodmaster's Monstrosity ability in a 1v1 situation against an opponent at 28hp. With available mana (3 Forests + 3 Islands + Sol Ring = ~7 mana), they could activate Monstrosity for X=3, creating 3 3/3 Hydra tokens doubled to 6 by Adrix and Nev (18 total power). This would create significant board pressure against DSV3 Stoic who only has Pristine Angel as a creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined all activated abilities including Hydra Broodmaster's Monstrosity
annotations.betterLine: Activate Hydra Broodmaster's Monstrosity for X=3, creating 6 3/3 Hydra tokens (doubled by Adrix and Nev) to build overwhelming board presence for the following turn
